_comment: Ad Hoc Session A3 -- built-in starter flag bundles for optimizer.py's --preset flag. Not a config format for user-saved presets (those live in the frontend's cloud-synced preset store, a separate mechanism) -- this file is the CLI's one-shot starting point for the three lineup types Greg builds: Cash, SE/3-Max GPP, and MME GPP (20-150 lineups). Any flag explicitly passed on the command line overrides the matching value here (see main()'s _load_preset_overrides()). lambda values are the validated defaults from Session 10.5b's backtest sweep (DK, 2018-2021, 65 weeks, holdout) -- see optimizer.py's --lambda help text and ROADMAP.md Ad Hoc Session A5. [UPDATED 2026-09-26: cash and se_gpp now use lambda=0 -- an 88-slate 2021-25 replay found 0.063 loses ~5 lineup pts vs 0 in all 6 seasons; see HANDOFF_fc_history_ownership_findings_2026-09-26.md. Original text follows.] Cash and se_gpp use lambda=0.063, the grid's best value for their own metric (cash beat@p44 +0.006 over 0.0, <1 SE, suggestive not conclusive; se_gpp/3-max beat@p50 also best at 0.063 but no clear winner over 0.0). mme_gpp uses lambda=-0.005, the grid's best value for large-field top@p90, where any positive lambda measurably hurts. mme_gpp's dart-exposure-cap/dart-floor-threshold (Ad Hoc Session A6, 2026-09-13) are a heuristic guard, NOT a swept/backtested value like lambda -- see optimizer.py's --dart-exposure-cap help text for the real Week 1 example (Kevin Austin Jr., a $3,000 near-zero-floor filler) that motivated it. Not added to se_gpp/cash: with only 1-3 lineups there's no meaningful 'exposure' to spread a dart across in the first place.

se3max_pool._comment: 2026-09-27: the 100-lineup SE3max candidate-pool build (pick-the-best-from-a-big-pool), separate from se_gpp's 3-lineup quick pick above. Settings match analysis/classic_diag/replay_batch.py exactly -- the test that found the best lineup in a 100-lineup pool lands at the 98th-99.9th percentile, graded against the real SE3max top-25% cash line (replay_validation.py's CASH_PCT=0.25). Confirmed against today's Week 3 pre-lock test builds (DK/FD main/early/afternoon).

showdown_se._comment: WK3 postmortem §2/§3 (2026-09-28, updated 2026-09-29 after a real-slate sanity check): the Showdown single-entry/Huddle counterpart to se_gpp. --stack-mode is intentionally omitted -- optimizer.py rejects it for Showdown pools (classic-only mechanism); Showdown stacking is handled entirely by the sd-* flags below. Evidence source: HANDOFF_showdown_lineupstudy_findings_2026-09-28.md + HANDOFF_showdown_construction_detail_2026-09-28.md, 142 real DK Showdown contests / 14.9M entries. sd-require-cpt-qb is Supported and hard in BOTH contest types (a WR/TE captain with no own-team QB in FLEX: -7.6 cash pts SE, -7.7 big, 0.60-0.69x return). The other three sd-* weights are lighter here than in showdown_gpp because the underlying evidence is weaker in single-entry: sd-qb-partner-bonus reflects RB partner being only Weak-to-Supported in SE (TE partner is Supported at +8.5, RB is Weak at +4.9-9.1 with a CI spanning 0 in the projection-controlled re-check) vs both Supported in big; sd-cheap-tier-penalty reflects the $600-1k tier being Weak-to-Supported in SE (CI touches 0 on cash lift, only the top-1% cut clears 0) vs Supported in big; sd-stack-cap/-penalty reflects the QB stack-depth-at-2 finding being Weak-to-Supported in both, kept equal. lambda 0 is Confirmed (chalk tilt is Not supported once tested against OUR modeled pre-lock ownership, not just realized/hindsight ownership -- see the lineupstudy doc's Task 1 replay). sd-exclude-cpt-positions/sd-k-cpt-penalty were ADDED 2026-09-29: the first version of this preset had no lever touching DST/K captaincy at all, and a 100-lineup sanity build on a real slate landed 21% of captains on K/DST despite Rule 3 (DST captain Supported-bad in both contest types). DST is now hard-excluded from CPT; K gets a soft penalty since its evidence is only Weak. These sd-* weights are first-pass point-scale conversions of cash-lift/return findings, NOT a backtested-swept calibration like lambda's own grid (Session 10.5b) -- treat as a starting point to validate against real Wk4+ Showdown results, same as any other track-2 item.

showdown_gpp._comment: WK3 postmortem §2/§3 (2026-09-28, updated 2026-09-29 after a real-slate sanity check): the Showdown large-field/MME counterpart to mme_gpp -- maps to the FC Lineup Study's 'big' contest type (150-max mini-MAX GPPs), not literally 'you build 100+ lineups'. --stack-mode omitted, same reason as showdown_se. sd-require-cpt-qb: same hard Supported finding as SE (-7.7 cash, 0.76x return). sd-qb-partner-bonus is higher here than SE because both RB (+4.9-5.8, Supported once projection/salary-controlled) and TE (+8.5-10.0, Supported) partners are on firmer footing in big-field data. sd-cheap-tier-penalty is higher here because the $600-1k tier is cleanly Supported in big (-2.6 cash, 0.82-0.83x return, 4/4 seasons) vs only Weak-to-Supported in SE. sd-stack-cap/-penalty: same Weak-to-Supported QB-stack-depth finding as SE. lambda stays 0 -- the realized-ownership chalk-tilt edge (+0.44 capped-return gap in big GPP) was real in hindsight but did NOT survive re-testing against our own modeled pre-lock ownership (+0.08, CI crosses 0; see the lineupstudy doc's Task 1) -- our Showdown ownership model only correlates 0.56 with the real field, so it isn't an actionable lever yet, not just an unvalidated one. sd-exclude-cpt-positions/sd-k-cpt-penalty were ADDED 2026-09-29 for the same reason as showdown_se -- a 100-lineup sanity build on a real slate (dk_showdown_wk2_NYG_LAR_21Sep2026) landed 15 K and 6 DST captains out of 100 with the pre-fix preset. Same first-pass-calibration caveat as showdown_se: validate against real Wk4+ results before treating these exact weights as final.
